data.title: The Wave Continues to Build
data.ai_summary: Two new privacy class action cases filed in late July 2026 demonstrate that AI-related wiretap litigation is accelerating and expanding into workplaces and restaurant telephone systems. In Chamberlain v. Granola, Inc., a plaintiff alleges the company's AI notetaking application secretly intercepted Microsoft Teams and Zoom communications without consent, advancing a novel theory against non-party class members. In Thompson v. SoundHound AI, Inc., a plaintiff alleges the company's restaurant phone AI intercepted calls before any human greeting, routing communications through SoundHound's servers for real-time transcription. Both cases raise novel legal questions around federal statutory claims and consent requirements that organizations deploying AI voice tools must consider.
